title: Overflow Smell
prompt:
**Scenario.** You must count pairs i < j in an array of n = 100000 elements; the count can reach ~5·10^9. Your comparator uses `a - b < 0` on values up to 10^9. What is the primary risk?

**Which approach is the best fit? The program only needs to print the letter.**

**A)** Neither — int handles 5·10^9 fine on 64-bit judges

**B)** The count needs int64 (long long), and the subtracting comparator can overflow int

**C)** Only the comparator is wrong; the count fits int

**D)** Both are fine; overflow is only a Java problem

tests.name: answer
tests.hint: 5·10^9 exceeds 32-bit range (≈ 2.1·10^9): count in long long. And subtracting two ints up to 10^9 can overflow int in the comparator — compare directly.
